{{short description|American politician}}
{{Use American English|date=July 2026}}

'''David W. Opitz''' is a former member of the [[Wisconsin State Assembly]] and the [[Wisconsin State Senate]].

==Early life==
Opitz was born on December 15, 1945, in [[Port Washington, Wisconsin]].<ref name=history>{{cite web|url=http://www.wisconsinhistory.org/dictionary/index.asp?action=view&term_id=2176&term_type_id=1&term_type_text=People&letter=O |title=Opitz, David W. 1945 |publisher=Wisconsin Historical Society |access-date=2013-10-25 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131013062456/http://www.wisconsinhistory.org/dictionary/index.asp?action=view&term_id=2176&term_type_id=1&term_type_text=people&letter=O |archive-date=October 13, 2013 }}</ref> He graduated from [[Carroll University]] and became a [[biologist]].

== Career ==
From 1971 to 1973, he served as Director of Environmental Health of [[Ozaukee County, Wisconsin]].<ref>{{cite book|editor=Wisconsin Legislative Reference Bureau |title=The State of Wisconsin 1979-1980 Blue Book |place=Madison |publisher=Wisconsin Department of Administration |year=1979 |page=60 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5SJWAAAAMAAJ&q=David+W.+Opitz%2BWisconsin%2BSenate&pg=PA60 |access-date=2013-10-25}}</ref> In 2019 Opitz was one of three plaintiffs in a suit filed in Ozaukee County District court that moved to hold Governor Evers of Wisconsin accountable to follow the law and require county clerks to clean the voter rolls every 30 days after receipt of a returned mailed postcard. Evers was ordering clerks to allow 200 days before cleaning up voter rolls. Local Judge [[Paul V. Malloy]] ordered that state law compelled him to order non conforming voter names of moved addresses be stricken from the voter rolls.<ref>[https://madison.com/wsj/news/local/govt-and-politics/conservative-legal-group-alleges-elections-commission-in-contempt-of-court/article_343fcbe4-050e-5679-8f30-3e2641a75567.html Conservative legal group alleges Elections Commission in contempt of court], ''[[Wisconsin State Journal]]'', Riley Vetterkind, January 2, 2020. Retrieved January 3, 2010.</ref><ref>[https://fox6now.com/2019/12/13/judge-orders-234000-voter-registrations-to-be-tossed/ Wisconsin judge orders removal of 234,000 voters from state registry], ''[[WITI (TV)|FOX6Now]]'', Amy Dupont, December 13, 2019. Retrieved January 3, 2020.</ref> Malloy refused to grant standing to the left leaning League of Women Voters, to intervene in the case.<ref name="Rothschild">[https://madison.com/ct/opinion/column/matthew-rothschild-elections-commission-is-right-to-hold-off-on/article_6c74c336-9fe3-59a4-9edb-a78580b5f5a1.html Matthew Rothschild: Elections Commission is right to hold off on voter purge], ''[[The Cap Times]]'', Matthew Rothschild, December 19, 2019. Retrieved January 3, 2020.</ref>

The Wisconsin Democracy Campaign, which Malloy also denied standing, also filed suit in federal court to halt the contested purging.<ref name="Rothschild" /> Wisconsin's Democratic Attorney General [[Josh Kaul]] also filed a notice of appeal to halt the voter roll updating, acting on behalf of the state's Elections Commission and requesting to stay of Malloy's order.<ref>[https://www.jsonline.com/story/news/politics/2019/12/17/wisconsin-voter-purge-elections-commission-appeals-judges-order-remove-from-rolls-league-of-women/2677466001/ Effort to stop removal of 234K voter registrations heads to federal court, while attorney general tries to stall purge in state court], Milwaukee [[Journal Sentinel]], Bruce Vielmetti and Molly Beck,  December 17, 2019. Retrieved January 3, 2020.</ref> The issue was brought before the court by the Wisconsin Institute for Law and Liberty (WILL).<ref name="Rothschild" /> The Institute is a Wisconsin organization mostly supported by the [[Bradley Foundation]], which funds such political causes.<ref name="Rothschild" /> The lawsuit demanded that the Wisconsin Election Commission respond to a "Movers Report," generated from voter data analysis produced by the [[Electronic Registration Information Center]] (ERIC), a national, non-partisan partnership funded in 2012 by the [[Pew Charitable Trusts]]. ERIC shares voter registration information to improve the accuracy of voter rolls.<ref>[https://www.pewtrusts.org/en/projects/archived-projects/election-initiatives/about/upgrading-voter-registration/eric Archived Project] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210308044637/https://www.pewtrusts.org/en/projects/archived-projects/election-initiatives/about/upgrading-voter-registration/eric |date=2021-03-08 }}, ''[[Pew Charitable Trust]]''. Retrieved January 3, 2020.</ref><ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2018/11/05/technology/unregistered-voter-rolls.html Another Use for A.I.: Finding Millions of Unregistered Voters], ''[[The New York Times]], Steve Lohr, November 5, 2018. Retrieved January 3. 2020.''</ref> The report tagged voters who may have moved to an address that had not yet been updated on their voter registration forms. Wisconsin may be forced to comply with Malloy's order.<ref>[https://slate.com/news-and-politics/2019/12/wisconsin-voter-purge-judge-order.html How a Conservative Group Persuaded a Judge to Purge Wisconsin's Voter Rolls], ''[[Slate Magazine]]'', [[Mark Joseph Stern]], December 16, 2019. Retrieved January 3, 2020.</ref>

On January 2, 2020, WILL said it asked the circuit court to hold the Elections Commission in contempt, fining it up to $12,000 daily, until it carries out Malloy's December 17, 2019, order to follow state law and purge from the voting rolls hundreds of thousands of registered voters who are confirmed to have moved to a different address, thus inflating the voter rolls. Those residents will need to register to vote at their new address. The case is being litigated in a state appeals court, but it was thought that the conservative leaning Wisconsin Supreme Court would be likely to hear it.<ref>{{cite news|last1= Vetterkind |first1= Riley |date= 2020-01-02 |title= Conservative legal group alleges Elections Commission in contempt of court |url= https://madison.com/wsj/news/local/govt-and-politics/conservative-legal-group-alleges-elections-commission-in-contempt-of-court/article_343fcbe4-050e-5679-8f30-3e2641a75567.html |work= [[Wisconsin State Journal]] |access-date= 2020-01-03 }}</ref> Ozaukee County is heavily Republican, having voted for a Democratic presidential candidate only once after 1936 when it voted for Lyndon Johnson in 1964.<ref name="Leip">{{cite web|url=http://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS|title=Dave Leip's Atlas of U.S. Presidential Elections|first=David|last=Leip|website=uselectionatlas.org|access-date=January 3, 2020}}</ref>

==Political career==
Opitz was elected to the Assembly in 1972. In April 1979, Opitz won a special election to the state Senate from the [[Wisconsin Senate, District 20|20th District]] and was reelected in 1980, remaining a member until 1984. He is a [[Republican Party of Wisconsin|Republican]].<ref name=history/> Opitz was appointed Chairman of the Wisconsin Republican Party by Gov. Tommy Thompson from 1990 to 1999.
